frase_inicial: Michael: let’s go step by step and start with one small thing.

tarjetas.reverso: If you set aside the home and the trip together, your bank cash would be gone and you’d have no easy cushion.
tarjetas.detalle: Current accessible cash $30,000; near-term cash needed $116,800; adjusted cash target $163,330–$172,636.

tarjetas.frente: Retirement won’t last to your plan end
tarjetas.reverso: Your savings are expected to run out before the plan ends, so some planned spending would be unpaid later in life.
tarjetas.detalle: Savings run out at age 85; planned unpaid spending $32,439.

tarjetas.frente: Life insurance is much smaller than your income needs
tarjetas.reverso: If your income stopped, the policy on file would leave a big gap for bills and debts that rely on you.

tarjetas.frente: No umbrella liability cover in the data
tarjetas.reverso: A big claim could touch the savings you’ve built, so check whether you already have cover or consider adding it.
tarjetas.detalle: Plan shows no umbrella; recommended minimum gap $1,000,000.

tarjetas.frente: Credit card is the most expensive debt
tarjetas.reverso: That card costs you the most interest; keeping the current monthly payment keeps the payoff on the schedule shown.
tarjetas.detalle: Card balance $3,500 at 20%, monthly $200, projected payoff July 2028.

tarjetas.frente: You’re saving a lot each year
tarjetas.reverso: Putting aside this amount is a real strength—your employer match is captured and it helps every long-term goal.
tarjetas.detalle: Total annual savings $43,000 including $7,000 employer match.

tarjetas.frente: Invested mix is a bit below your growth target
tarjetas.reverso: Your stock share is lower than the growth glide the plan targets; that’s something to review once cash needs are set.
tarjetas.detalle: Invested savings $145,000; current stock share ~74% versus glide toward 98%.

tarjetas.frente: A home purchase will change many numbers
tarjetas.reverso: Buying in January 2027 would add a mortgage and new housing costs that compete with saving and the cash cushion.
tarjetas.detalle: Planned purchase $566,500; down payment held $113,300; loan $453,200 at 7%, monthly payment $3,015.15.

tarjetas.frente: Your income is strong and gives options
tarjetas.reverso: With your salary and saving habit, you can choose which pressure to ease first—cash for the home, more retirement funding, or insurance.

movimientos.title: Add umbrella cover
movimientos.action: Add $1M of umbrella to raise the liability shield

movimientos.title: Lower the withdrawal rate
movimientos.action: Cutting withdrawals to $10,300/year (6.0%) reaches the sustainable band

movimientos.title: Raise growth allocation toward glide
movimientos.action: Move the invested mix from 74% to 88% growth (glide 98%) for the next horizon-fit band — about $19,900 of the invested book

mapa.aviso: Illustrative simulator: it shows the direction of change, not a Sherpas projection.

siguiente_paso.razon: The plan shows no umbrella in place and recommends adding a liability shield to protect your liquid savings and net worth before the house closes.
pasos: Open your email or insurer app and find your auto or renter policy number
Call or message your insurer and ask: “Do I have umbrella liability cover? If not, what’s the monthly premium to add $1M?”
Save their answer in a note and we’ll compare the premium to your budget together
